newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool Q1 seen boosting '97 performance.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool Q1 seen boosting '97 performance.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp expects its first-quarter results, to be released Wednesday, to contribute toward its goal of improved operating performance for the year, David Whitwam, chairman and chief executive officer, said in remarks delivered at the annual meeting Tuesday.
"Securities rules limit what I can tell you about the period," Whitwam said. "However, I will say I'm overall pleased with the quarter and the progress it represents toward our full-year goals."
The First Call mean estimate for first-quarter earnings of the Michigan-based appliance maker is $0.58 per share, up from $0.50 in the year-ago quarter.
For full-year 1996, the company's earnings, excluding a restructuring charge, declined from 1995 by 16 percent, to $175 million, or $2.33 per share.
Last year's "results from a poor European market were unsatisfactory, but bottomed out in the second quarter (of 1996) and have trended upward through the first quarter of 1997," Whitwam said.

The company, aided by new products, expects to gain market share even though North American industry shipments are expected to be down slightly in 1997, mostly because carryover air-conditioner inventories asre higher than usual, Whitwam said.
"Shipments in Brazil will slow somewhat from 1996, but should still grow by nearly a double-digit rate," he added.
Whirlpool will benefit from cost-reduction and productivity-improvement efforts at its manufacturing plants, from a better mix of products and brands and from stable total material costs, he said.

"In Asia, we expect solid operating improvement, at least in part, because 1997 will be the first full year of operation for all six of our regional joint-venture companies," Whitwam said in his remarks. Whirlpool was up 1/4 at 45-3/4.
